page: Amazon Web Services i7i.24xlarge is a storage-optimized server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processors using the x86_64 architecture. It features 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores with 2 threads per core) operating at 3.2 GHz, supported by a 320 MB L3 cache. The hardware configuration includes 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Storage is highly dense, featuring 22,500 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 56 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark testing, the i7i.24xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance, particularly in multi-threaded operations and data processing. It achieves top 10% placement in Passmark CPU scores (93,054.5), multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (552.44 GB/sec), and static web serving throughput (132.74 GB/sec). Single-core and multi-core Geekbench scores also rank in the top 10%, alongside ray tracing and software compilation benchmarks. Memory bandwidth is strong, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 6,647.85 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 119.97 GB/sec. Database performance is highlighted by a strong Passmark database operations score of 32,606.17 and Redis SET operations processing 113.26 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the i7i.24xlarge offers high resource density by bundling massive local NVMe storage directly with a substantial memory footprint and high-core-count compute resources. This eliminates the need for external storage attachments for high-throughput workloads, though the lack of a dedicated GPU limits its efficiency for heavy parallel deep learning training. The server is optimized for large-scale databases, high-throughput web serving, data compression tasks, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
